geometry_edits.rationale: Widen the street-side notch to make the access edge read as a more legible public threshold.
Deepen the cut so the frontage becomes a more meaningful void rather than a shallow incision.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant bar with a secondary notch/cut, and it is legible in all four views rather than only one. The parcel containment appears respected, and the mass does not show obvious collisions across views. The blue frontage is addressed only moderately: there is some seam/notch logic, but the ground response is still more sealed than openly public. Program-wise, the compact bent-bar language is plausible for neighborhood living, but the section remains somewhat generic and not strongly expressive of a public threshold or a clear occupied void. The silhouette is coherent but slightly code-like in its step/clip treatment rather than exceptionally capacity-bearing. Overall it is viable, with room to strengthen the access edge and carve a more useful public void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger campus-complex complexity than this compact candidate; do not copy the multi-wing scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking rectilinear masses with a central void and clear upper/lower hierarchy can support neighborhood mixed-use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much smaller and more single-story than the candidate; useful only for access/threshold logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple pavilion with a strong entry canopy and crisp ground threshold can reinforce active frontage.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual vertical section logic is more residential-waterfront than this street-facing neighborhood brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/stepped massing can work when it preserves a coherent base and makes a legible public edge.

warnings: No visible thin green parcel boundary or blue frontage is perfectly centered in every view; assessment assumes the displayed guide geometry is the parcel/access contract.
The section/roof logic is acceptable for neighborhood living, but the public-ground relationship could be more explicit.
Some apparent depth changes may be view-dependent; no hard collision across views is evident.
